notes: Prompts never name the skill, so the with_skill runs also test triggering (check the transcript for a Skill call with skill=shibroui). Baselines are told not to use shibroui. Audit-based assertions are graded by running shibroui/scripts/audit.js on the output page at 1280x900, with the modal/sheet opened where stated.

evals.name: invoices-card-build
evals.prompt: I'm building the billing area of my SaaS app. Can you make me a single self-contained HTML file (plain HTML/CSS plus a little vanilla JS, no frameworks or CDNs) for an "Invoices" card: a search box with a Search button, a table of 6 invoices (client, invoice number, issue date, amount in USD, status: paid / pending / overdue), simple pagination under the table, and a Delete action on each row that opens a confirmation modal. Light theme, clean and modern. Save it as <outputs>/invoices.html
evals.expected_output: A single invoices.html that follows shibroUI: right-aligned tabular amounts, text status badges, equal control heights, visible focus, adequate targets, and a modal with scrim, elevation and focus handling.

assertions.text: The run invoked the shibroui skill on its own (transcript shows Skill tool with skill=shibroui)
Audit: no SU-45/SU-46 contrast failures
Audit: no SU-17 findings (amount column and its header right-aligned, text columns not centered)
Audit/code: amount cells use tabular-nums (no SU-16 finding)
Code: each status shows a visible word (Paid/Pending/Overdue), not color alone
Audit: no SU-58 finding (search input and button share a height)
Audit: no SU-59/SU-60 findings
Audit: no SU-70 findings (2px+ visible focus ring)
Audit: no SU-61/62/65/69 fail-level findings
Code: the per-row Delete is low emphasis (text/ghost/icon), not a filled loud button
Audit with the modal open: no SU-103 findings (shadow + dimming backdrop)
Code: modal moves focus inside, closes on Escape and returns focus (showModal or equivalent)
Audit: no SU-78 finding (reduced-motion fallback when motion is used)
Audit: no SU-93 findings

evals.name: settings-review-fix
evals.prompt: Here's our workspace settings page: <inputs>/settings.html. Something about it feels off and a few users complained it's hard to use. Can you review it for UI/UX problems and then make a fixed version? Keep the same content and features. Write the fixed page to <outputs>/settings-fixed.html and your review to <outputs>/review.md, listing each problem you found and what you changed. Don't modify the original file.
evals.expected_output: A review that catches the planted problems (ideally citing rule IDs with measurements) and a fixed page with zero audit fails.

assertions.text: The run invoked the shibroui skill on its own
Review flags the low-contrast hint text (#9ca3af on white)
Review flags the white label on the yellow button
Review flags inputs that blend into the card (no fill/border)
Review flags removed focus outlines
Review flags the 24px icon buttons / tight spacing
Review flags the 32px search input next to the 40px button
Review flags the checkbox whose text is not a clickable label
Review flags the color-only status dot
Review flags centered table columns / numbers not right-aligned or tabular
Review flags the centered intro paragraph and/or the over-long line length
Review flags the vague 'click here' link and/or the non-underlined inline link
Review flags the press animation (0.84 scale, 700ms, linear) and/or the ±30px shake
Review flags the cover's radius equal to the card's radius
Review flags Delete account being as loud as Save / too many primary buttons
Review flags inconsistent naming (Workspace / Organization / team)
Review flags the bare 'No results.' empty state
Review flags label-to-field gap equal to field-to-field gap
Audit of settings-fixed.html: zero fail-level findings
Fixed page keeps the same sections, fields, table rows and actions

evals.name: share-sheet-motion
evals.prompt: I have a simple article page (<inputs>/article.html). Add a "Share" button that opens a bottom sheet with three share options (Copy link, Email, X) and a close button, and when someone picks Copy link show a small "Link copied" toast at the bottom. I want the animations to feel really nice and snappy. Write the result to <outputs>/article.html (leave the original alone).
evals.expected_output: Interruptible transition-based sheet and toast with short durations, role-appropriate easing, reduced-motion fallback, scrim, elevation, 44px targets and proper focus handling.

assertions.text: The run invoked the shibroui skill on its own
Code: sheet open/close is driven by CSS transitions / WAAPI / springs that can reverse mid-flight, not one-shot @keyframes
Audit: no SU-85 findings; code durations ≤ 350ms for sheet and toast
Audit: no SU-82 findings; enter uses an ease-out style curve
Audit: no SU-72 findings (press scale within 0.95–0.98 if present)
Audit: no SU-78 finding
Audit with the sheet open: no SU-103 findings (scrim + elevation)
Audit with the sheet open: no SU-65/SU-61 fail-level findings
Code: Escape closes the sheet and focus returns to the Share button
Code: the toast uses role=status or aria-live
Audit with the sheet open and after the toast: no SU-45/SU-46 failures
